lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Check that the portfolio or profile link is active and professional.
items.because: If the contact information is anonymized for this review, no change is needed.

items.says: Consider adding GPA, honors, relevant coursework, or finance activities if they strengthen the résumé.
items.because: With a 2020 graduation date, these are optional and do not replace relevant experience.

items.says: Clarify the period covered by the average of about five rounds a week.
Keep the caddie duties concise if targeting finance positions.
items.because: Carrying bags and reading greens may use valuable space unless the experience shows relevant skills or fills a timeline gap.

items.says: Specify your responsibility and the tournament’s scale.
items.because: “Helped” is vague and does not show what you contributed.

items.says: Define “close efficiency” and give its before-and-after baseline.
items.because: The review cannot tell whether the 40% measures elapsed close time, hours spent, or something else.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the automation and whether it caused the 40% improvement.
Explain what decisions or outcomes the capital-plan analysis informed.
Clarify whether teams adopted the shared template.
items.because: The stated benefit does not establish that teams used it.

items.says: Clarify what “each line more than 5% off budget” includes.
items.because: It could mean every variance above the threshold or all lines in the pack.

items.says: Explain the basis for the 5% threshold and your role in preparing the commentary.
The valuation description discounts free cash flow to equity at WACC.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity is normally discounted at the cost of equity, not WACC.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins is not a valid way to calculate the group margin.
items.because: The group margin should be calculated from aggregated EBITDA and revenue.

items.says: Define how forecast error was calculated and over what period.
Clarify whether the forecast enabled the USD 40M repayment.
items.because: The repayment may merely have happened afterward.

items.says: The cash-flow achievement appears again under the Student Investment Fund.
items.because: Both roles may not legitimately claim the same achievement.

items.says: Give the observation period and clarify whether every approved loan completed its first two years.
items.because: The zero-default claim may include loans that have not yet had time to default.

items.says: Explain your underwriting role versus the final approval decision.
Give the declined-application sample size and explain how the two ratio thresholds changed.
State the period over which approvals rose from 41% to 48%.
Define the period and comparable basis for “no rise in early defaults.”
Avoid implying the findings caused the approval and default outcomes unless you can support that attribution.
“Writes” uses present tense in an ended role.
items.because: It conflicts with the surrounding past-tense bullets.

items.says: Explain whether you created, maintained, or used the checklist.
Define “missed covenant tests” and the comparison period for the reduction from 7 to 1 per year.
Give the basis for the six-to-three-hour comparison, including whether it covers multiple memos.
Clarify whether you built the template yourself or adapted an existing one.
Identify the valuation date and the market-price date used for comparison.
Explain the context for the result within 6% of market price.
items.because: That proximity does not by itself demonstrate model quality.

items.says: State the base discount rate.
Clarify whether the one-point change was an increase or decrease and which direction produced each value.
Describe your contribution to the pitch and whether the club used the model, the note, or both.
items.because: “Used it in its spring pitch” does not make your role or the use clear.

items.says: Explain which organization “the FP&A team” refers to and how the work fits the fund role.
items.because: The description sounds inconsistent with the listed Student Investment Fund role.

items.says: Clarify what you rebuilt and which benchmark or return measure the report used.
Verify the timeframe and consistency of the committee’s use of the report.
items.because: “Used at every meeting” is a broad claim.

items.says: The cash-forecast bullet closely duplicates the Stonebridge achievement.
items.because: The matching forecast horizon, error rate, and debt repayment amount create a major credibility risk across two roles.

items.says: Indicate your proficiency or the specific Excel and Bloomberg Terminal functions you can use.
items.because: The tools line currently gives no indication of either.

items.says: Support each listed method with a specific example elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: The listed methods are broad.

items.says: Consider additional methods needed for target roles, but only ones you have used.
